newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger, eye on Bank of Canada.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger, eye on Bank of Canada.

text.p: Canadian bonds rallied to close higher on Friday, boosted by strong foreign interest after a week of positive news, analysts said.
"In Canada we outperformed versus the U.S. again," said Toronto-Dominion Securities fixed income analyst Arve Bendiksrud.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond jumped C$0.70 to C$107.20 to yield 7.377 percent, compared to the U.S. 30-year benchmark, which rose 16/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
The spread between the two was flat at 55 basis points from Thursday's close, at its lowest point since 1985.
Many market players had forecast Canada's central bank would drop short-term interest rates at 0900 EDT (1300 GMT), but the Bank of Canada defied expectations and kept the bank rate steady.

Canada's currency eased after weaker-than-expected unemployment data this morning. September's unemployment rate spiked to 9.9 percent from a month earlier 9.4 percent. Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast 9.3 percent.
"The Canadian dollar weakened off slightly following the report, which may have discouraged the Bank from cutting rates this morning," said a Bank of Montreal market commentary.
The unit softened to C$1.3522 (US$0.7395) from Thursday's close of C$1.3503 (US$0.7406) which was near a year high.

"However, the dollar firmed up later in the morning while the money market has already factored in a 25-basis points rate cut," the report said. "Thus we believe the Bank will ratify the market's expectations following the Thanksgiving weekend."
All Canadian markets will be closed for Monday's holiday.
Today the bond market closed early at 1500 EDT (1900 GMT).
This week Finance Minister Paul Martin reaffirmed that the government was on its way to eliminating the deficit by 2000.
Bank of Canada governor Gordon Thiessen said the currency had room to appreciate without harming its competitiveness.
"We had the foreign buying through the morning," one trader said. "People still love Canada."

In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.55 to C$102.24 to yield 6.69. 10-year benchmark gained 16/32 to yield 6.85 percent. The spread between the two stayed flat at 16 basis points from Thursday's close, at an 11-year low. The three-month cash bill traded at 3.41 percent against the U.S. one at 5.14 percent.
